newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to refine 22 mln t oil '97 vs 13 mln '96.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to refine 22 mln t oil '97 vs 13 mln '96.

text.p: Ukraine's six oil refineries will refine up to 22 million tonnes next year, compared to 13 million tonnes in 1996, a senior government official said on Friday.
"Next year we will refine 20-22 million tonnes of oil on Ukrainian territory," Anatoly Mynchenko, state minister responsible for the energy and industrial sectors, told Reuters.
"This year we refined nine million tonnes of Russian oil and four million tonnes of our own oil."
He said Ukraine had adequate energy reserves for this winter and there would be no energy crisis.
The annual capacity of Ukraine's refineries was about 60 million tonnes in the Soviet era.
Mynchenko said six million tonnes would be refined at the Kremenchug refinery in central Ukraine through a Ukrainian-Russian joint venture.
Another six million tonnes would be refined at eastern Ukraine's Lisichansk refinery, the second largest, whose total capacity is 16 million tonnes.
The remaining four refineries are set to process six million tonnes of Russian oil, delivered under a 1994 agreement that obliged Moscow to supply that amount of oil until 2000.
They will also refine about four million tonnes of Ukraine's domestic output.
